\begin{theorem}[quotient group]\label{thm:quotient}
Let $N\trianglelefteq G$, and let $G/N$ be the set of cosets $gN$. The rule
\[
(aN)(bN)=abN
\]
is well defined and makes $G/N$ a group, with identity $N$ and $(aN)^{-1}=a^{-1}N$. The projection $\pi:G\to G/N$, $g\mapsto gN$, is a surjective homomorphism with kernel $N$. If $G$ is finite, $|G/N|=|G|/|N|$.

Conversely, if $N\le G$ and the rule above is well defined, then $N$ is normal.
\end{theorem}

entries.claim:
\begin{theorem}[P\'olya's counting theorem]\label{thm:polya}
Let a finite group $G$ act on a finite set $X$, let $k\ge1$ be an integer, and for $g\in G$ let $c(g)$ be the number of cycles of the permutation $\rho_g$ of $X$. The number of colourings of $X$ with $k$ colours, up to the action of $G$, is
\[
\frac1{|G|}\sum_{g\in G}k^{c(g)}.
\]
More precisely, give each colour $c$ a weight $w_c$ (a variable), and a colouring $f$ the weight $w(f)=\prod_{x\in X}w_{f(x)}$. If $g$ has $c_j(g)$ cycles of length $j$, the sum of the weights of one colouring per orbit is
\[
\frac1{|G|}\sum_{g\in G}\ \prod_{j\ge1}\Big(\sum_{c}w_c^{\,j}\Big)^{c_j(g)}.
\]
\end{theorem}

entries.claim:
\begin{theorem}[Gauss]\label{thm:countirr}
For $n\ge1$, let $N_q(n)$ be the number of monic irreducible polynomials of degree $n$ over $\mathbb F_q$. Then
\[
\sum_{d\mid n}d\,N_q(d)=q^n,\qquad N_q(n)=\frac1n\sum_{d\mid n}\mu(d)\,q^{n/d},
\]
and
\[
\Bigl|N_q(n)-\frac{q^n}n\Bigr|<\frac{2q^{n/2}}n.
\]
In particular $N_q(n)\ge1$ for every $n\ge1$.
\end{theorem}

entries.claim:
\begin{theorem}[fundamental theorem of Galois theory]\label{thm:ftgt}
Let $L/K$ be a Galois extension with group $G$.
\begin{enumerate}[label=(\alph*)]
\item The maps $H\mapsto L^H$ and $M\mapsto\operatorname{Gal}(L/M)$ are inverse bijections between the subgroups of $G$ and the intermediate fields $K\subseteq M\subseteq L$. They reverse inclusions, and
\[
[L:L^H]=|H|,\qquad[L^H:K]=[G:H].
\]
\item For $\sigma\in G$, $\sigma(L^H)=L^{\sigma H\sigma^{-1}}$.
\item $M/K$ is Galois iff $\operatorname{Gal}(L/M)$ is normal in $G$. Then restriction $\sigma\mapsto\sigma|_M$ induces an isomorphism $G/\operatorname{Gal}(L/M)\cong\operatorname{Gal}(M/K)$.
\end{enumerate}
\end{theorem}
